Keywords: War elephants in the Amida siege
RagShortTexts: Elephants served at Amida in 359 and required handlers, fodder and passable ground.

Variants.Content: Elephants deployed with other troops when the Persian coalition besieged Amida in 359, their size making a powerful impression on defenders. They still needed handlers, fodder and water. Walls, ditches and crowded approaches restricted movement; elephants did not replace siege engines and infantry.

Soldiers facing elephants needed to follow commands and avoid crowding companions in panic. Handlers had to watch the animals’ reactions and footing. A passage blocked by men and horses made the animals’ size a hindrance to turning.

Using elephants required food, water and passable routes, followed by coordination with archers, infantry and engines. Their intimidating appearance did not mean a gate had been breached, and congestion could prevent them from being used effectively.
